input: "Darkness, Aqua — you two go check the sewer entrance. Scouting only. Aqua, your water magic might actually be useful for once, and Darkness, you can... enjoy yourself. I'll register the quest with Luna and we'll catch up."

messages.content:
Aqua sets her fourth mug down with a hollow *thunk* and stares at you like you've just asked her to scrub a latrine with her own scepter. The morning light catching the foam on her upper lip somehow makes the expression worse.

Darkness, by contrast, has gone very still. Her gauntlets clench against the tabletop, and a deep flush is already climbing her neck — you can practically hear her imagination sprinting ahead to dark water, crushing jaws, the exquisite helplessness of being dragged under while her party is too far away to save her. Her breath catches audibly.

Megumin doesn't even lift her cheek from the table. One crimson eye opens halfway, tracking the conversation with the weary resignation of a fourteen-year-old who vaporized a hillside at dawn and now can't feel her own spine. She exhales something that might be a laugh, or just the last of her mana leaving her body.

Across the hall, Luna is already watching your table with the fixed, pleasant smile of a woman who knows exactly which quest you're about to claim and has been waiting all morning for someone — anyone — desperate enough to take it.

The sewers?! Kazumaaaa, I am a goddess! A goddess does not wade through other people's filth just because you're too lazy to— wait. You said my water magic might actually be useful. ...Fine. But you're buying me the expensive wine when we get back. Not the cheap stuff. The bottle with the gold foil. (crosses her arms, then uncrosses them as the compliment registers — preening despite herself)
messages.speaker: Aqua

messages.content: The sewers. Where the Brutal Alligators are. You want me to go first. Alone with Aqua. Into a confined underground passage where anything could be lying in ambush, where I'd have no choice but to throw myself between danger and a goddess who can't fight... Kazuma, this is — this is an outrageously irresponsible order and I accept it completely. (already rising from her seat, cheeks flushed, breath quickening with every word)
messages.speaker: Darkness

messages.content: While you two charge into the dark to be grappled by reptiles, I shall remain here and guard this table. With my body. Which is currently fused to this bench by the sacred exhaustion of a true explosion master. Do not wait for me. (does not move; one finger lifts weakly from the table in a gesture that might be a salute)
messages.speaker: Megumin

input:
"Megumin, guard the table with your life. I'm going to make sure those two haven't already gotten themselves eaten."

I push back from the table and head for the door, ignoring whatever Luna was about to say, and make my way toward the sewer entrance.

messages.content:
You push back from the table. The legs scrape across worn floorboards, and Luna's head snaps up from behind the counter — she was mid-sentence, a parchment already half-extended toward you, her professional smile frozen in the act of dying.

The door swings open. Axel's morning light floods the threshold, dusty and golden, and then you're through it, the heavy oak thudding shut behind you. Luna's outstretched hand hangs in the air for a beat too long before it drops to her side. The parchment curls inward on itself like a dead leaf.

Megumin remains exactly where she is, slumped sideways in her chair with one arm draped dramatically over the table. Chomusuke has materialized from somewhere and is kneading the small of her back. She cannot feel her legs. She cannot stand. She cannot chase after you. Her crimson eyes track the closed door with an expression that is sixty percent outrage and forty percent something she would never, ever name aloud.

Luna turns to look at her. Then at the door. Then back at Megumin. The silence in the guild hall is the special kind that only follows after one of *your* parties — the other adventurers at distant tables are very pointedly not watching, the way people don't watch a cart crash into a fruit stand.

He left me! Me, the foremost genius of the Crimson Demon Clan, reduced to a table-guardian while those two go gallivanting toward certain digestive peril! The indignity sears hotter than my Explosion's afterglow! (attempts to rise, gets approximately two inches off the chair, and collapses back down with a wheeze)
messages.speaker: Megumin

messages.content: He didn't even let me finish. I had the quest scroll. Right here. In my hand. That man has walked away from me four times this week and it's only Tuesday. (lets the parchment drop onto the counter, her professional smile twitching at the corner)
messages.speaker: Luna

input:
I come to a stop in front of the open grate, the sewer's damp breath rolling up over my boots. I kneel at the edge and focus, letting my Enemy Detection skill hum through the darkness below.

"...Alright. Let's see what's waiting for us down there."

messages.content:
Your boots scuff against the stone lip of the open grate as you come to a halt. The air here is thick with mildew and something older — stagnant water that hasn't seen sunlight in decades. Aqua stands a deliberate three paces back from the edge, her feather mantle pulled tight around her shoulders like a shawl against the cold, though the morning isn't cold at all. Darkness is right at the rim, one armored boot nearly over the drop, gripping her sword hilt with both hands. Neither of them has noticed you yet.

You kneel. The skill hums to life behind your eyes — a prickling pressure that reaches down into the dark like an outstretched hand. For a moment there's nothing but the drip of water echoing up from somewhere deep. Then the pings start.

Three of them. Large. The first two are clustered together maybe thirty yards down the main tunnel, sluggish — basking, probably. The third is moving. Slow, sinuous, the signature dragging itself through the water toward the junction directly below the grate. Each ping carries the distinct oily weight of predation: cold-blooded, patient, hungry. Definitely Brutal Alligators. Definitely big ones. Your skill can't tell you much more than that — size and number and direction — but you've been at this long enough to know what "big and moving toward the only entrance" means.

Well?! Don't just kneel there making dramatic faces, Kazuma! How many are down there? If it's more than one I'm not going first. I refuse. A goddess does not wade into — ugh, this smell is going to stick to my robes for weeks, I just know it. (She pinches her nose with two fingers and leans forward just enough to peer into the darkness, then immediately recoils.)
messages.speaker: Aqua

messages.content: Three... you're sensing three, aren't you? I can tell by the way your jaw tightened. Kazuma, please — please tell me they're the kind that grab you from below and drag you under before you can scream. (Her voice starts formal and breathless, then drops to something almost reverent. She shifts her weight forward, the grate groaning under her boot.)
messages.speaker: Darkness

input: I rise from my knee, dusting the grit off my hands. "Three of them. Two are lounging thirty yards down — lazy, for now. The third one's moving toward the junction right below us." I glance back at Aqua, still pinching her nose three paces back. "Aqua, go back to the guild and grab rope and lanterns. If we're going in, we're not doing it blind."

messages.content:
Aqua's pinched fingers drop from her nose. For the first time since you arrived at the grate, something other than theatrical disgust flickers across her face — it takes you a beat to recognize it as hope. The feather mantle settles around her shoulders as she straightens, already half-turned back toward the guild.

Darkness has not moved. She remains at the rim of the grate, gauntlets locked around her sword hilt, staring down into the dark like a woman staring into a lover's window. Her breath comes shallow and uneven, and when she finally lifts her gaze to you, her cheeks are flushed a deep, splotchy crimson that has nothing to do with the morning chill.

The sewer below gurgles. Something heavy scrapes against stone — the junction alligator, restless.
